topic: Global cavity re-pressurization (SAA synchronous decay) — c3 re-review verifying c2 patches
our_argument_summary: WIN-057b argues that the dome-claimed "Global Cavity Re-Pressurization" — inferred from synchronous magnetic decay at three INTERMAGNET stations (labeled TTB/VSS/HER in the dome text, with TTB being the dome's own mislabel for what should be TSU Tsumeb, Namibia) — is standard MHD geophysics relabeled. Terra-Nova et al. (2017) derive SAA splitting from CMB reversed-flux patches; Alken et al. (2021, IGRF-13) document the SAA field state at epoch 2020.0. The synchronous decay is expected because the stations sit within the SAA's spatial correlation length. The dome has no mechanism for "cavity rupture" and the claim substantially duplicates evidence already counted in WIN-004/005/035/041. Verdict: Std Model Explains.

holes_found.description: Attribution overreach in the Alken IGRF-13 sentence. Current text reads: "Alken et al. (2021, IGRF-13) further document the SAA's second minimum emerging near 20°S, 10°E (matching the dome's 'Lobe B') as a natural consequence of reverse-flux patch migration". The IGRF-13 paper (10.1186/s40623-020-01288-x) is a model definition paper — per its own abstract, it provides "the equations defining the IGRF, the spherical harmonic coefficients... maps of magnetic declination, inclination and total field intensity for the epoch 2020.0". Field maps at epoch 2020.0 do show the second minimum near 20°S, 10°E, so the DOCUMENTATION-OF-THE-OBSERVATION part is defensible. But the mechanistic attribution "as a natural consequence of reverse-flux patch migration" is really Terra-Nova et al. 2017 (already cited earlier in the paragraph) or Rother et al. 2020 (10.1186/s40623-020-01277-0, "recent evolution of the South Atlantic Anomaly", cited BY IGRF-13 as its ref 37). A defender could parse the sentence as attributing the causal mechanism to IGRF-13 itself, which would be a mischaracterization. The IGRF-13 model paper does not itself argue for reverse-flux patch migration as the cause.
holes_found.recommendation: Two options: (1) Tightening (preferred, keeps citation): rephrase to "Alken et al. (2021, IGRF-13) provide the field maps for epoch 2020.0 that show the second minimum's emergence near 20°S, 10°E — a natural consequence of the reverse-flux patch dynamics Terra-Nova et al. document." This preserves both citations and correctly attributes the mechanism to Terra-Nova. (2) Replacement: swap the "further document" citation from Alken IGRF-13 to Rother et al. 2020 (10.1186/s40623-020-01277-0), which is titled "recent evolution of the South Atlantic Anomaly" and explicitly addresses SAA structure and evolution rather than being a global model coefficient paper. Either fix is fine; the first is smaller change and keeps IGRF-13 in the citation set as its field-maps role is legitimate.

holes_found.description: TLDR-evidence carries forward the dome's station labels ("Three INTERMAGNET stations (TTB, VSS, HER)") without the disambiguation callout. This is defensible for a TLDR — the technical dispute about IAGA codes belongs in the detail, and TLDRs are simplifications for non-science readers per project TLDR conventions (severity minor at most, don't flag imprecision that doesn't mislead). No hole raised on this if the reader-facing simplification threshold applies. Recording as minor because a strict reader could argue the TLDR reproduces the mislabel without any signal that the detail-view carries a caveat. Below the "actual mischaracterization" bar in the curmudgeon TLDR review guidance; noted for completeness only.
holes_found.recommendation: No change required — the current TLDR is within the "imprecision that does not mislead" tolerance zone. If the operator wants a stricter posture, one option is to add a five-word parenthetical like "(TTB is the dome's mislabel)" but that hurts TLDR readability. Recommend leave as-is.

stronger_arguments.description: Northern-hemisphere absence argument (originally raised in c1 stronger_arguments, still not incorporated into detail_evidence). The dome's own claim is a "global" cavity re-pressurization at r ≈ 20,000 km — yet the three cited stations sit in a ~70°-longitude southern-hemisphere band (Namibia, Brazil, South Africa, all within the SAA cell region). A genuinely cavity-scale structural change should produce detectable correlated signals at Northern Hemisphere and Pacific INTERMAGNET stations too (BOU Boulder, KAK Kakioka, GUA Guam, HON Honolulu). The absence of any such multi-hemisphere corroboration in the dome's own evidence undermines the "global" framing without additional argumentation. This is a first-order counter to the "cavity rupture" claim: the dome asserts a global effect but supplies only regional data.
sources: INTERMAGNET GIN station registry (BOU, KAK, GUA, HON coordinates)
stronger_arguments.recommendation: Consider adding a sentence to detail_evidence in the "Why it fails" section: "The dome's own three-station evidence set (Namibia, Brazil, South Africa) all sits inside a single southern-hemisphere longitude band within the known SAA cell region — a 'global' cavity effect should also register at Northern Hemisphere and Pacific INTERMAGNET stations (BOU, KAK, GUA, HON), and no such multi-hemisphere corroboration is presented." This would make the argument more airtight against a defender pointing out that "global" claim is asserted but not supported by the station geography.

stronger_arguments.description: The "r ≈ 20,000 km" ↔ disc_radius=20,015 km numerological match (c1 stronger_arguments[1], still not addressed in detail_evidence). The dome claims the "Ovoid Shoulder shift" occurs at r ≈ 20,000 km — essentially identical to the dome's own disc_radius parameter of 20,015 km. This places the claimed structural rupture at the disc edge, which in dome geometry is near the Antarctic ice wall / disc rim, an area of maximum geometric distortion. The numerical closeness is presented as if it were a prediction, but it is a tautology: the dome model defines r ≈ disc_radius as the geometric extremum, so any rupture "at the shoulder" is definitionally at r ≈ 20,000 km. Non-derivation dressed as prediction.

kernel_of_truth.description: The SAA has genuinely bifurcated into two intensity minima (wins.json:057b:detail_evidence "dome author correctly identifies the dual-lobe structure and its spatial coordinates"), and INTERMAGNET stations across southern Africa and eastern South America really do show correlated secular variation. These are real geophysical observations from a real monitoring network. Alken et al. 2021 IGRF-13 (10.1186/s40623-020-01288-x, this-run CrossRef-verified) provides the epoch-2020.0 field maps that show precisely the second-minimum emergence the dome cites.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: The observation is standard MHD, not a dome discovery. Terra-Nova et al. 2017 (10.1016/j.pepi.2017.03.002, this-run CrossRef-verified, "Relating the South Atlantic Anomaly and geomagnetic flux patches") derives the SAA dual-lobe structure and multi-station correlation from core-mantle boundary reversed-flux patches. The dome relabels the mechanism ("Ovoid Shoulder shift at r ≈ 20,000 km") without deriving anything from its own geometry (wins.json:057b:code_analysis: derives_from_dome=false), and the underlying INTERMAGNET evidence substantially duplicates what is already counted in WIN-004/005/035/041 — the dome's own detail_evidence explicitly names those four WINs as the overlap set.

deeper_analysis: This is a c3 re-review of the c2 findings after decider self-apply (decider-2026-07-22T02-11, patch file suggested-patches-2026-07-22T02-10.json). Two of three c2 holes were closed by field patches (ISS-3007 station-code disambiguation callout added to detail_claim; ISS-3008 DOI swapped from editorial to substantive primary paper). One (ISS-3009 detail_group mismatch) was wontfixed per c1's original low-priority framing. Both fixes are text-verified and citation-verified. Two fresh c3 minor holes: (a) the Alken IGRF-13 sentence in detail_evidence reads as if IGRF-13 itself argues for reverse-flux patch migration as the causal mechanism, which is a slight overreach — IGRF-13 provides the field maps that show the observation, but the mechanistic causal attribution properly belongs to Terra-Nova 2017 (already cited) or Rother 2020. (b) TLDR still uses raw "TTB" label without callout, defensible under TLDR simplification norms. Two stronger_arguments from c1 remain unincorporated into detail_evidence: the Northern-hemisphere-absence counter to the "global" framing, and the disc_radius↔"r ≈ 20,000 km" numerological match. These are stronger_arguments not holes — the current text is defensible without them but would be more airtight with them.
